paper.title_en: Improved <math><mi>β</mi></math>-decay properties of the <math><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>105</mn></mrow></math> isobars from Rh to Mo
paper.abstract_en:
Background: Recent studies of the β decay of fission fragments by total absorption spectroscopy have found less decay energy attributed to leptons than previously believed, with studies of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Tc</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> being particularly impactful for reactor decay heat. These results are also crucial for interpreting measurements of reactor antineutrino energy spectra.
Purpose: To obtain complete <math><mi>β</mi></math>-decay patterns of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Tc</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ru</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rh</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. Determine the impact on reactor decay heat for all four isotopes and the impact on <math><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>e</mi></msub></math> emission calculation for <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Tc</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>.
Method: The complete <math><mi>β</mi></math>-decay intensities of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Tc</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ru</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rh</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> were measured with the Modular Total Absorption Spectrometer (MTAS) at Argonne National Laboratory. A beam of radioactive isobars with mass number A = 105 was produced by the CARIBU source and delivered to MTAS. Specifically, for <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, a multireflection time-of-flight device was employed to isolate a pure beam of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nuclides before delivery to MTAS. Highly-efficient silicon <math><mi>β</mi></math>-trigger has substantially aided the purification of the collected spectra.
Results: The mean <math><mi>β</mi></math> and <math><mi>γ</mi></math> energies of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Tc</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> are found to be consistent with previous TAS measurements. Differences are found in the extracted <math><mi>β</mi></math>-feeding intensities in commonly used evaluations of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Tc</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, which results in substantial differences in reactor antineutrinos detectable via inverse <math><mi>β</mi></math> decay. Improved half-lives for <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ru</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> are also determined.
Conclusions: The number of reactor antineutrinos detectable via inverse <math><mi>β</mi></math> decay for <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> is found to decrease by 86%, while a 37% increase is found for <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Tc</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. An improved precision in the half-lives of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ru</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> has been determined to be 4.4644(13) h, and 35.5(8) s, respectively.
